stories.h: Anti-APC 'Bamayi' chant triggers clash on campaign convoy in Gombe
stories.e: An APC campaign convoy touring Balanga South in Gombe State came under attack after local youths greeted it with chants of "Bamayi", a local expression of rejection, sparking a violent confrontation that damaged five campaign buses and left several party supporters injured. No fatalities were recorded, and those behind the attack had not been identified by the time of reporting, as the incident unfolded during the party's campaign tour ahead of the 2027 general elections.

stories.h: NAFDAC uncovers expired baby diapers and balms in Lagos store raid
stories.e: Nigeria's drug and food regulator raided a Lagos store and found diapers, methylated balms, baby wipes and other items that had been expired since 2022, alongside unregistered goods. NAFDAC evacuated the products and said it was investigating how they remained in storage and circulation for years, and who had intended to distribute them.

stories.h: Defence Headquarters denies supplying uniforms seen in bandits' viral video
stories.e: The Defence Headquarters has rejected claims that military camouflage uniforms shown in a viral video of suspected bandits originated from the Nigerian armed forces, with spokesman Major General Michael Onoja ruling out the possibility entirely. He also dismissed suggestions that the clothing was looted from attacked military supply vehicles, saying no such incident had been reported, amid long-running concern over unauthorised use of military-style uniforms by criminal gangs.

stories.h: FCT health workers' union threatens strike over unpaid allowances
stories.e: The Joint Health Sector Union's FCT chapter has given the Federal Capital Territory Administration a seven-day ultimatum, expiring 23 November, to pay outstanding allowances owed to healthcare workers under the Consolidated Health Salary Structure. The union says the administration has for three months failed to extend a professional allowance table already granted to colleagues on a different salary structure, calling the disparity discriminatory and unfair.

stories.h: Amnesty International condemns Kano council chair over calls for election violence
stories.e: Amnesty International has publicly condemned Abubakar Mojo, chairman of Gwale Local Government in Kano State, after a widely circulated video showed him urging APC supporters to use intimidation and violence to win their polling units ahead of the 2027 elections. The rights group branded him a "danger to society" and called on the authorities to hold him to account, while also criticising security agencies for failing to act against politicians who threaten electoral violence.

stories.h: EFCC arraigns woman over alleged N1.1bn NNPC job appointment fraud
stories.e: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission has arraigned Halimat Adenike Tejuosho before the Federal Capital Territory High Court in Gwagwalada, accusing her and a co-defendant of defrauding a woman of over N600 million between 2024 by falsely promising to secure her appointment as Group Managing Director of the NNPC. She pleaded not guilty to a five-count charge, and the court ordered her to deposit her international passport pending further proceedings, adjourning the case to February.

stories.h: ASUU renews demand for unpaid 2022 salary arrears
stories.e: The Academic Staff Union of Universities has again demanded that the federal government pay lecturers' salary arrears dating back to 2022. The long-running dispute highlights ongoing questions about the government's management of public sector wage obligations in the education sector.

stories.h: Yiaga Africa urges INEC to publish guidelines for 28 November mock accreditation
stories.e: Civic group Yiaga Africa has called on the Independent National Electoral Commission to make public the rules governing its planned mock accreditation exercise on 28 November. The organisation says clear, published guidelines are essential for transparency and public confidence as Nigeria prepares further electoral reforms ahead of 2027.

stories.h: State health budgets jump 67% to over N3.3 trillion, minister demands results
stories.e: Nigeria's state governments have raised their combined health budgets by 67 per cent to more than N3.3 trillion in 2026, Health Minister Muhammad Pate told the National Council on Health. Pate flagged weak accountability, noting that 44 per cent of the council's previous resolutions were never implemented, and ordered states to submit quarterly progress reports.

stories.h: Court warns Attorney-General could face jail over Okuama release order
stories.e: A Nigerian court has threatened to commit the Attorney-General of the Federation to prison for failing to comply with an order to release persons connected to the Okuama case. The warning intensifies pressure on the federal government to respect judicial rulings in a matter that has drawn sustained public scrutiny over the rule of law.

stories.h: Yiaga Africa demands INEC publish guidelines for 2027 mock accreditation exercise
stories.e: Civil society group Yiaga Africa has urged the Independent National Electoral Commission to immediately release the framework and polling unit list for its nationwide mock accreditation and results-upload test scheduled for 28 November. Executive director Samson Itodo said withholding the details could shut out citizens, parties and observers from scrutinising the BVAS and IReV technologies ahead of the 2027 general election.

stories.h: Nigeria Air fraud trial: cross-examination of EFCC witness continues against Sirika
stories.e: The corruption trial of former aviation minister Hadi Sirika, his daughter Fatima, her husband Jalal Hamma and a linked firm resumed in Abuja, with defence lawyers cross-examining an EFCC investigator over contracts awarded during Sirikas tenure. Prosecutors allege Sirika awarded a 1.5 billion naira Katsina airport contract and a 1.3 billion naira Nigeria Air consultancy deal to firms tied to his family and associates. The case was adjourned to 15 December.

stories.h: Army admits holding talks with armed bandits in Kwara after viral video
stories.e: The Nigerian Army has confirmed that troops engaged in dialogue with armed bandits in Kwara State's Edu council area, following a viral video that showed soldiers interacting with the group and prompted public outcry. Army spokesman for Operation Savannah Shield, Ibrahim Shittu, said the contact was a deliberate strategy to recover weapons and free captives rather than fraternisation, reporting that 10 kidnap victims were freed and 12 AK-47 rifles recovered. The episode has renewed debate over the transparency of the military's mixed approach of negotiated surrenders alongside offensive operations against armed groups.

stories.h: Offa robbery: Kwara court rules Saraki, Ahmed cannot be arraigned without proper service
stories.e: A Kwara State High Court has ruled that former Senate President Bukola Saraki and ex-governor Abdulfatah Ahmed cannot be arraigned over the 2018 Offa bank robbery until they are properly served with the charges, rejecting the state government's bid to proceed immediately. The defence had argued that serving only the defendants' lawyers did not meet due-process requirements. Saraki and Ahmed deny any link to the robbery, which killed more than 30 people, and describe the renewed prosecution as politically motivated.

stories.h: INEC to distribute 78,112 new PVCs in Enugu, rules out collection by proxy
stories.e: Nigeria's electoral commission says it has received 78,112 newly produced Permanent Voter Cards for distribution across Enugu State's 17 local government areas, covering first- and second-phase registrants as well as transfers and replacements. The state's Resident Electoral Commissioner, Chukwuemeka Chukwu, insisted the cards would only be handed to their rightful owners and not released by proxy, while appealing to parties, community leaders and the media to encourage prompt collection ahead of the 2027 polls.

stories.h: ICPC resists bail for man accused of posing as PFIPC director-general
stories.e: The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission has opposed bail for a suspect accused of impersonating a director-general at the disputed presidential agency PFIPC, arguing he is safer remaining in custody. The case forms part of a wider controversy over the agency's legitimacy and leadership.

stories.h: CCB witness details price gap in Ozekhome-Useni London property trial
stories.e: A Code of Conduct Bureau official testified in the forgery and impersonation trial of senior lawyer Mike Ozekhome and Ponfa Useni, telling the court that Useni's declared 1992 purchase price for a London property fell far short of the £200,000 a UK tribunal had found. The witness said the gap could not be explained by Useni's declared income, and the case was adjourned to 23 November.

stories.h: Senate demands sanctions over deaths of 37 miners in NSCDC custody
stories.e: Nigeria's Senate has called on the federal government to prosecute or sanction NSCDC officers found responsible for the deaths of 37 suspected illegal miners who died in the agency's custody in Niger State in September, and to compensate their families. A federal investigative panel attributed the deaths to asphyxiation, and the Senate President cautioned colleagues against assuming the detainees were guilty of any crime.

stories.h: Reps summon NAFDAC, police, SSS over deaths linked to herbal drug
stories.e: The House of Representatives has summoned officials from NAFDAC, the police and the SSS to explain how they are tackling fake and dangerous drugs, after an unregistered herbal product reportedly killed four people and sickened others in Benue State between late October and November. Lawmakers said NAFDAC's roughly 2,000 staff are far too few to police the market, and called for a nationwide probe and tougher penalties for sellers of unregistered remedies.

stories.h: Tinubu receives State Police Bill after all 36 assemblies approve it
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu has received the constitutional amendment bill to establish state police forces, after all 36 state houses of assembly ratified it, exceeding the required two-thirds threshold. The bill, already passed by the Senate and House of Representatives, will be reviewed with the Attorney-General before Tinubu formally signs it. A separate national policing bill, still being drafted, will set out the legal and operational framework for the new state forces alongside the federal police.

stories.h: Opposition coalition postpones unity pact signing to 30 November
stories.e: A six-party coalition seeking to challenge President Bola Tinubu in 2027, including the ADC, APM, NDC, a PDP faction, the PRP and the SDP, has pushed back the signing of its planned cooperation agreement by a week to 30 November. Coalition figure Salihu Lukman said the delay followed consultations with party leaders and presidential candidates over clashing campaign schedules, though the group's hardest unresolved question, whether to back a single presidential candidate, remains unsettled.

stories.h: ADC questions Tinubu's reliance on World Bank over fuel subsidy removal
stories.e: African Democratic Congress spokesperson Bolaji Abdullahi has accused President Tinubu's administration of prioritising World Bank recommendations over the welfare of Nigerians in removing the petrol subsidy, arguing the institution was never elected to govern the country. He cited rising public debt and debt-servicing costs, and urged government to cut spending on aircraft, yachts and convoys before asking citizens to endure further hardship.

stories.h: Soludo hands Tinubu APGA's presidential flag ahead of 2027 polls
stories.e: Anambra State Governor Charles Soludo, national leader of the All Progressives Grand Alliance, formally presented the party's presidential flag to President Bola Tinubu at a campaign rally in Awka, with Vice-President Kashim Shettima receiving it on the president's behalf. Unlike in 2023, APGA is not fielding its own presidential candidate for 2027, having opted instead to back Tinubu's re-election bid.

stories.h: Obi cannot win presidency without cross-regional support, says Shettima
stories.e: Vice-President Kashim Shettima, campaigning for President Tinubu's re-election at a rally in Awka organised by Governor Charles Soludo, argued that NDC candidate Peter Obi's Igbo heritage alone will not secure him the presidency and that he needs alliances beyond the South-East. He urged Igbo voters to look past ethnic sentiment, drawing a comparison with Muhammadu Buhari's earlier failed bids before his cross-regional win in 2015.

stories.h: Kano council chair under fire after urging APC supporters to secure polling units by hook or crook
stories.e: A viral video showed Gwale local government chairman Abubakar Mojo telling APC supporters to win their polling units peacefully or through strife, and warning rivals ahead of the 2027 elections. Amnesty International condemned the remarks as incitement and called for him to be held accountable, while he maintains his Hausa comments were mistranslated.

stories.h: Court dismisses Atiku's bid to amend suit challenging Tinubu's 2027 eligibility
stories.e: A Federal High Court judge in Abuja, Inyang Ekwo, rejected an application by Atiku Abubakar and the African Democratic Congress to amend their suit alleging the APC submitted a forged NYSC discharge certificate for President Tinubu to INEC, ruling that the proposed changes fell outside the 14-day window allowed for pre-election cases. The underlying suit, which seeks to bar Tinubu from the 2027 ballot, now proceeds to a full hearing.

stories.h: Ebonyi APC rejects 'rainbow coalition', insists state remains fully APC
stories.e: The All Progressives Congress chapter in Ebonyi State has rejected suggestions of a multi-party 'rainbow coalition', insisting the state remains firmly under APC control. The statement comes amid wider jostling among Nigerian political parties ahead of the 2027 general election.

stories.h: Court affirms Yahaya Bello as APC's Kogi Central senatorial candidate
stories.e: A Nigerian court has dismissed a suit seeking to disqualify former Kogi governor Yahaya Bello from standing as the APC's senatorial candidate for Kogi Central. The ruling clears the way for Bello's candidacy to proceed despite the corruption allegations that continue to trail him.

stories.h: Soludo says Tinubu does not need to rig the 2027 election to win
stories.e: Former Anambra governor Charles Soludo has argued that President Tinubu does not need to manipulate the outcome of the 2027 election, saying his record in office will be enough to secure victory. The remarks add to an increasingly public debate among politicians over whether the 2027 polls will be credible.

stories.h: Sule Lamido criticises Vice-President Shettima as Jigawa PDP launches 2027 campaign
stories.e: Former Jigawa governor Sule Lamido accused Vice-President Kashim Shettima of careless public remarks unbefitting his office, including past jibes at Atiku Abubakar and Yemi Osinbajo, and warned he risks becoming a political liability for the APC. Lamido made the comments as the PDP formally presented its 2027 election candidates in Jigawa, insisting the party is quietly rebuilding despite claims that it has become irrelevant.

stories.h: Tinubu expands 2027 campaign visits to 19 states and the FCT
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu's re-election campaign has widened his planned rally appearances from 12 to 19 states plus the Federal Capital Territory, according to APC national publicity secretary Felix Morka. He is now expected to attend 20 of the 37 rallies planned nationwide between October 2026 and January 2027, with Katsina, Taraba, Zamfara, Imo, Kwara and Abuja newly added to his itinerary.

stories.h: Anambra government defends removal of billboard showing Peter Obi
stories.e: Anambras government has confirmed pulling down a campaign billboard that featured NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi alongside senatorial candidate Victor Umeh, who owns the signage. Officials say the billboard was removed because Umeh had not paid the required fee and had used it to promote a presidential candidate in breach of the states Signage Act, denying any link to Obis image or political affiliation.

stories.h: Court throws out suit challenging Yahaya Bellos APC senatorial ticket
stories.e: A Federal High Court in Abuja has struck out a suit by senatorial aspirant Momoh Obaro seeking to overturn former Kogi governor Yahaya Bellos APC ticket for Kogi Central. Justice Inyang Ekwo ruled that Obaro had gone to court without first exhausting the partys internal dispute-resolution process, and that his result sheets lacked the required signatures. Bello still faces separate corruption trials over his tenure as governor.

stories.h: APC, ADC and NDC trade blame over campaign violence claims
stories.e: The ruling APC accused the opposition ADC and NDC of sponsoring protests and an attack on President Tinubu's motorcade in Abuja, while the ADC denied the claims and demanded evidence. The NDC separately questioned an N11.2 trillion NNPC 'other receivables' balance, calling for a forensic audit of the figure.

stories.h: Tinubu receives state police bill after all 36 assemblies give assent
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu has received a constitutional amendment bill allowing states to set up their own police forces, after all 36 state houses of assembly approved it, well above the required two-thirds threshold. He is expected to consult the Attorney-General before signing it at a formal ceremony, while a separate national policing framework bill is still being finalised.

stories.h: ADC denies sponsoring violence, challenges APC to produce evidence
stories.e: The African Democratic Congress has rejected APC claims that it and the NDC are sponsoring violence and recruiting youths to disrupt ruling-party campaign events, calling the allegations a distraction from economic hardship under President Tinubu. The ADC's campaign council asked why the APC has not named or prosecuted any alleged sponsors, deepening tensions between the parties ahead of the 2027 elections.

stories.h: ADC lodges 17-ground appeal against INEC over Atiku's disqualification
stories.e: The African Democratic Congress has filed a 17-ground appeal challenging the Independent National Electoral Commission's nullification of Atiku Abubakar's candidacy for the 2027 presidential race. The party is seeking to overturn the decision through the courts ahead of the election.

stories.h: Senate directs clerk to forward State Police bill to Tinubu for assent
stories.e: The Senate has instructed the National Assembly clerk to transmit the amendment bill establishing state police to President Bola Tinubu for his signature. Lawmakers also urged the executive to forward a separate National Policing Bill to the National Assembly, as Nigeria moves towards decentralising policing.

stories.h: Jonathan warns of political violence and ethnic divisions ahead of 2027 polls
stories.e: Former President Goodluck Jonathan has cautioned that rising political intolerance, violence and ethnic rivalry could threaten Nigeria’s stability as the country heads towards the 2027 general election. Speaking at a peace and security conference organised by his foundation in Abuja, he warned that political parties and campaign groups were beginning to resemble cult-like structures that recruit young people as instruments of violence. He also flagged conflicting court rulings as a risk to public confidence in the judiciary.

stories.h: ADC demands evidence after APC accuses opposition of sponsoring thugs
stories.e: The ADC Presidential Campaign Council rejected APC claims that it sponsored disruptions of ruling-party rallies, with spokesperson Phrank Shaibu arguing the governing party cannot make such allegations without producing evidence or naming and prosecuting suspects. Shaibu pointed to inconsistent APC and presidency statements on whether Tinubu's convoy was actually attacked, and in turn called for scrutiny of reported cash distribution at APC campaign events.

stories.h: FG to roll over unspent 2026 capital budget into 2027
stories.e: The Federal Ministry of Finance says it will carry forward unspent 2026 capital spending into the 2027 budget, moving towards a single annual budget cycle. Coordinating Minister of the Economy Taiwo Oyedele announced the plan after an Economic Management Team meeting in Abuja, which also reviewed the 2027 Finance Bill and a 90-day plan to stabilise food prices.

stories.h: Joblessness drives over a quarter of new Nigerian businesses in 2026 - report
stories.e: The Fate Institute's State of Entrepreneurship report, unveiled in Lagos, found that 26.5 per cent of new businesses launched in 2026 were started mainly because founders could not find jobs rather than to pursue a specific opportunity. The report found overall business growth rose to 75 per cent from 67 per cent a year earlier, while persistent power shortages and skill gaps continue to limit productivity.

stories.h: FG domestic borrowing hits 110% of 2026 annual target by September
stories.e: A report by the Financial Markets Dealers Association shows the Federal Government's net domestic borrowing reached N20.32 trillion by the end of September 2026, about N1.92 trillion above the N18.4 trillion target set for the whole year in the 2026 budget. The report also found domestic debt-service payments rose roughly 21 per cent quarter-on-quarter to about N2.6 trillion, as total public debt stood at N166.79 trillion as of June 2026.

stories.h: Otti presents N1.2trn 2027 budget to Abia Assembly
stories.e: Abia State Governor Alex Otti has presented a N1.2 trillion appropriation bill for 2027 to the state House of Assembly, an 18 per cent rise on the current year's budget, with about 80 per cent earmarked for capital projects. The governor said roughly N552.67 billion of the budget would be funded through concessional loans, while lawmakers promised a line-by-line review before passage.

stories.h: Nigerian stocks lose N3 trillion in three days as Dangote Cement, Aradel and banks tumble
stories.e: The Nigerian Exchange's All-Share Index fell from a record 254,763 points to 248,286 points over three sessions, with Dangote Cement down nearly 10 per cent and Aradel Holdings hitting its daily trading limit. Analysts attributed the slide to profit-taking, investors freeing up cash ahead of the Dangote Petroleum Refinery's planned listing, falling oil prices and a weakening naira.

stories.h: Abia governor presents N1.2trn budget for 2027
stories.e: Governor Alex Otti has presented a N1.2 trillion appropriation bill for 2027 to the Abia State House of Assembly, an 18 per cent rise on this years budget. About 80 per cent is earmarked for capital projects, with education and healthcare taking the largest shares of planned social spending, while over N552 billion is expected to come from concessional loans tied to infrastructure.

stories.h: Government to curb raw mineral exports as mining revenue tops N100bn
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu has said Nigeria intends to move away from exporting unprocessed solid minerals, calling instead for investment in local processing and beneficiation to grow domestic industry and jobs. Speaking at a mining investment summit in Abuja, Solid Minerals Minister Dele Alake said sector revenue had climbed from just N6 billion a year before the current administration to over N100 billion in 2026, crediting digitisation and a crackdown that has seen over 300 illegal operators apprehended.

stories.h: Jumia cuts workforce by 3% as it pushes toward profitability
stories.e: E-commerce group Jumia trimmed its workforce by about 3 per cent in the third quarter of 2026 as part of a broader push to reach profitability. The cuts reflect continuing cost pressures facing technology and e-commerce firms operating across the Nigerian and wider African market.

stories.h: Dangote Refinery expands IPO by 30% to widen investor allotment
stories.e: Dangote Refinery has increased its planned initial public offering by 30 per cent, a move expected to improve allotment prospects for retail investors applying for shares. The expanded offer underscores strong demand for one of Nigeria's largest industrial listings in recent years.

stories.h: Economists say Nigeria's GDP growth has yet to translate into shared prosperity
stories.e: Speaking at the 2026 National Growth and Development Forum in Abuja, Nigerian Economic Society president Baba Yusuf Musa said improving indicators such as 4.43 per cent GDP growth, falling inflation and record external reserves have not yet reached ordinary citizens. He noted that roughly nine in ten Nigerian workers remain in the informal economy and about 63 per cent of the population still lives below the poverty line, and called for job-creating growth and disciplined public finance.

stories.h: Nigerians can now apply for N100 million federal mortgage loans at 9.75%
stories.e: The federal governments MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund is now accepting applications from Nigerians for mortgages of up to N100 million at a fixed 9.75 per cent interest rate over 20 years, President Tinubu announced. Applicants must be at least 21, meet income and credit checks, and pay a minimum 10 per cent deposit; the fund says more than 2,300 Nigerians across 27 states have accessed N160 billion so far.

stories.h: Dangote Refinery raises IPO target to $2.1bn after $4.5bn in bids
stories.e: Dangote Petroleum Refinery has increased its share offer target from $1.6 billion to about $2.1 billion after receiving nearly $4.5 billion in investor applications, with Nigerian retail and pension investors expected to get priority allocation. The expanded offer, still subject to SEC approval, will help fund the refinery's planned capacity increase to 1.4 million barrels per day.

stories.h: FG, states and councils share N2.441trn October revenue
stories.e: The federal, state and local governments shared N2.441 trillion from the Federation Account for October 2026, continuing the regular monthly allocation process overseen by the three tiers of government. The disbursement reflects Nigeria's ongoing dependence on centrally collected revenue to fund public spending.

stories.h: Abuja's Agura Hotel shut down over alleged N155m tax debt
stories.e: The Nigeria Revenue Service has sealed the long-running Agura Hotel in Abuja over an unpaid tax debt dating from 2010 to 2015, which it says stands at roughly N155 million. Hotel management say they were paying down the balance but were sealed without fresh notice, halting operations and forcing it to send staff home while it seeks documents to negotiate further with the agency.

stories.h: NLC and TUC resolve dispute over N70,000 transport allowance
stories.e: Organised labour's two main centres, the NLC and TUC, have settled their disagreement over the implementation of a N70,000 transport allowance for workers, ending a standoff that had threatened industrial action. Details of how the resolution will be applied across the public sector are still emerging.

stories.h: Care economy could create 17 million jobs and add $9.3bn to GDP, report finds
stories.e: A new report estimates that investing in Nigeria's care economy, covering childcare, eldercare and domestic work, could generate about 17 million jobs and add $9.3 billion to the country's GDP. The findings highlight the sector's largely unrecognised economic contribution, much of it currently unpaid and performed by women.

stories.h: Headline inflation eases to 14.06% in October as food prices tick back up
stories.e: The National Bureau of Statistics said headline inflation slowed to 14.06 per cent year-on-year in October 2026, down from 14.63 per cent in September, even as food inflation worsened on a month-on-month basis. Imo recorded the highest headline rate at 28.66 per cent and Taraba the lowest at 6.12 per cent, and analysts quoted in the report cautioned that the improving figures are not yet being felt in households' day-to-day costs.

stories.h: States yet to draw down most of $500m World Bank NG-CARES top-up
stories.e: The Federal Government and the World Bank said $490 million of a $500 million additional financing package for the Nigeria COVID-19 Action Recovery and Economic Stimulus programme remains undisbursed to states, and urged participating states to speed up implementation. Officials said 17 states have submitted eligibility documents for clearance while six others are preparing theirs, as the programme continues to fund social protection, food security and small-business support.

stories.h: Nigeria demands $1.3trn annual climate finance at COP31
stories.e: At the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkiye, Nigeria's Environment Minister Balarabe Lawal called on developed nations to make the global target of $1.3 trillion in annual climate finance by 2035 genuinely accessible and affordable to developing countries. He also pressed for cheaper concessional financing and faster implementation of the Loss and Damage Fund, while citing Nigeria's new National Adaptation Plan and a $300 million renewable energy fund.

stories.h: Elumelu raises Seplat stake to 22% with fresh $70m share buy
stories.e: Businessman Tony Elumelu, through his Heirs Energies vehicle, has bought about 5.9 million additional shares in Seplat Energy worth roughly $70 million, lifting his combined interest in the oil and gas company to around 22.1 per cent. The purchase follows an earlier September acquisition and comes ahead of Elumelu taking over as Seplat's board chairman from January.

stories.h: Tax authority sets 30 November deadline for crypto operators to register
stories.e: The Nigeria Revenue Service has ordered individuals and businesses engaged in virtual asset activities to register on its newly launched Virtual Asset Service Provider Tax Portal by 30 November, with full technical integration due by 31 December. The agency says the move, backed by the 2025 Nigeria Tax Administration Act, is meant to strengthen tax compliance and support anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorism-financing checks across crypto exchanges, custodians and payment platforms operating in or serving Nigeria.

stories.h: Nigeria's payment system retains status as Africa's only 'mature' system - report
stories.e: The AfricaNenda Foundation's 2026 State of Inclusive Instant Payment Systems report found Nigeria's National Instant Payment system remains the only one on the continent rated 'mature', a status it has held since 2025. The report credited the system's identity verification and consumer recourse mechanisms, while warning of rising payment fraud across Africa more broadly.

stories.h: FCMB Group doubles nine-month profit to N272.8bn on margin growth
stories.e: FCMB Group's profit before tax more than doubled to N272.8 billion for the nine months to September 2026, driven by stronger net interest margins and digital revenue growth. Profit after tax rose to N232.9 billion, lifting the lender's nine-month return on equity to 30 per cent, with the chief executive signalling full-year returns could exceed earlier guidance.

stories.h: Naira slips to eight-month low against the dollar
stories.e: The naira closed at N1,388 to the dollar on Thursday, its weakest level since early March, as official exchange-rate data from the Central Bank showed a further slide to N1,376.58. Interbank foreign exchange turnover jumped by nearly 60 per cent from the previous day, reflecting a sharp rise in dollar demand this week.

stories.h: CBN, NNPC sign deal to tighten oil revenue oversight, boost forex inflows
stories.e: The Central Bank of Nigeria and state oil firm NNPC have signed a memorandum of understanding aimed at tightening oversight of oil and gas revenue and channelling more foreign exchange through official channels. Under the agreement, NNPC will align its domestic payments and contractor settlements with CBN rules, while the central bank sets up a dedicated unit to manage the oil firms transactions and support the naira stability.

stories.h: Naira weakens to N1,379.99/$ as interbank FX turnover tops $500 million
stories.e: The naira depreciated to N1,379.99 against the US dollar as interbank foreign exchange turnover exceeded $500 million in a single trading session. The movement highlights continuing volatility in Nigeria's market-driven exchange rate regime.

stories.h: NNPC to leverage assets for fresh capital under new CBN arrangement
stories.e: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company plans to use its assets as collateral to raise capital under a new agreement with the Central Bank of Nigeria. The arrangement raises fresh questions about transparency in how the state oil company finances its operations and obligations.

stories.h: NNPC, CBN sign MoU to tackle forex challenges, strengthen energy financing
stories.e: NNPC Ltd and the Central Bank of Nigeria have signed a memorandum of understanding aimed at deepening cooperation between the energy sector and the financial system, group chief executive Bayo Ojulari announced. The agreement covers joint efforts to ease foreign exchange pressures, help export earnings flow back into the economy, and develop financing structures that let NNPC raise capital against its own balance sheet under CBN guidance, replacing what Ojulari described as a pattern of one-off requests to the apex bank.

stories.h: NGX sheds N642bn as investor caution deepens mid-week losses
stories.e: The Nigerian Exchange's All-Share Index fell by about 0.4 per cent, wiping roughly N642 billion off market capitalisation, as heavy selling hit large and mid-cap stocks including Zenith Bank and Aradel Holdings. Analysts expect continued profit-taking to limit any near-term recovery.

stories.h: Naira slips as seasonal dollar demand strains CBN's reserves
stories.e: The naira weakened to around N1,363 per dollar on the official market, its lowest in 18 days, as foreign exchange inflows fell sharply and external reserves dipped from their October peak. Analysts linked part of the pressure to foreign investors pulling out of Nigerian short-term debt amid rising developed-market yields.

stories.h: Dangote Refinery raises planned IPO size to $2.1bn on strong investor demand
stories.e: Dangote Refinery has increased the size of its planned initial public offering to $2.1 billion after investors expressed demand worth $4.5 billion, signalling strong appetite for the company's shares. The upsized offering reflects growing confidence in Nigeria's largest refining asset ahead of its listing.

stories.h: Tinubu unveils N100m mortgage scheme at fixed 9.75% rate
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu has announced that Nigerians can now access mortgages of up to N100 million at a fixed interest rate of 9.75 per cent, repayable over 20 years with a 10 per cent initial deposit, funded through the N1 trillion MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund. He said more than 2,300 Nigerians across 27 states have already accessed N160 billion through the scheme, and stressed that applicants need no political connections to qualify.

stories.h: Nigerian banks cut impairment charges by 47% after costly loan clean-up
stories.e: Impairment charges at eight major Nigerian lenders fell by about 47% in the first nine months of 2026, as banks worked through a costly clean-up of bad loans from previous years. The decline points to improving asset quality across the banking sector, though analysts caution that credit risk could resurface given broader economic pressures.

stories.h: DMO allots N1.42trn at November bond auction as yields fall
stories.e: Nigeria's Debt Management Office allotted N1.42 trillion in federal government bonds at its November auction, with yields declining as investor demand stayed strong. The result points to ample liquidity in the financial system but also underscores the government's continued heavy reliance on domestic borrowing to fund its budget.

stories.h: NGX Group buys 10% stake in Nairobi Securities Exchange
stories.e: Nigerian Exchange Group has completed the purchase of a 10% shareholding in the Nairobi Securities Exchange, extending a pan-African strategy that already includes a stake in Ethiopias bourse. Group executives say the move diversifies NGXs returns beyond Nigeria and deepens integration across African capital markets.

stories.h: Nigeria's dollar turnover rises 89.17% to $3.42 billion as spot transactions rebound
stories.e: Foreign exchange turnover in Nigeria's official market jumped 89.17 per cent to $3.42 billion, driven by a rebound in spot dollar transactions. The surge points to improving liquidity in the currency market even as the naira continues to face pressure from global and domestic demand.

stories.h: NGX Group buys 10% stake in Nairobi Securities Exchange
stories.e: Nigerian Exchange Group has acquired a 10 per cent equity stake in Kenya's Nairobi Securities Exchange, extending its push into East African capital markets. The deal follows NGX Group's earlier investment in the Ethiopian Securities Exchange and forms part of a wider pan-African strategy to diversify beyond the Nigerian market.

stories.h: DMO offers N2tn in bonds as banks' liquidity surplus hits N3.97tn
stories.e: Nigeria's Debt Management Office is offering N2 trillion in federal government bonds at its November auction, up from N1.75 trillion in October, reopening four existing instruments maturing between 2028 and 2033. The offer comes as Central Bank data show banking-sector liquidity surplus reaching roughly N3.97 trillion, with analysts projecting further inflows from maturing treasury bills and OMO bills.

stories.h: Nigeria's foreign reserves shed $391m in 16 days, sharpest fall in six months
stories.e: Central Bank of Nigeria data show gross external reserves fell by roughly $391 million over 16 days to $54.87 billion by 12 November, the steepest such decline since April. Despite the recent slide, reserves remain about $9.3 billion higher than at the start of the year, helped by a slower but still positive monthly accretion in October.

stories.h: CBN survey shows Nigerian banks loosened credit conditions in third quarter
stories.e: A Central Bank of Nigeria credit conditions survey found that lenders widened access to secured, unsecured and corporate loans in the third quarter of 2026, with approval rates rising across all three categories. Demand for credit also increased, while default rates fell, even though overall private-sector credit dipped slightly between August and September. The findings follow the CBN's 350-basis-point cut to its benchmark rate in September, its largest reduction in two decades.

stories.h: Regulator flags 13 high-risk oil wells in Rivers gas seepage probe
stories.e: The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission says 13 of 28 oil and gas wells it screened near a gas seepage site in Bille community, Rivers State, are high risk, with inspectors finding active gas leaks, corrosion and vandalism at several facilities. The regulator is now running geochemical tests to trace the source of the emissions and has warned that residents may need to be evacuated if the seepage turns out to be a natural geological event.

stories.h: Yutong to build CNG bus assembly plant in Ibadan under federal transport initiative
stories.e: Chinese bus maker Yutong, the world's largest by sales volume, is to establish a compressed natural gas bus assembly plant in Ibadan in partnership with the Presidential Initiative on CNG and Electric Vehicles. The deal, which supports a federal programme aiming to cut transport fares by about 40 per cent on participating routes, will see an initial batch of 300 buses supplied, with the first 100 reaching Lagos by the end of December 2026.

stories.h: Chinese bus giant Yutong to build CNG assembly plant in Ibadan
stories.e: Yutong, described as the worlds largest bus manufacturer, has agreed to set up a compressed natural gas bus assembly plant at the former Leyland Automotive site in Ibadan, under Nigerias Presidential Initiative on CNG and Electric Vehicles. The firm will initially supply 300 CNG buses, with the first 100 expected in Lagos by December, as part of a push to cut transport fares by around 40 per cent on participating routes.

stories.h: Nigerian drugmakers raise factory investment 81% to N29.26bn
stories.e: Nigeria's five listed pharmaceutical manufacturers increased capital spending by 81 per cent to about N29.26 billion in the first nine months of 2026, channelling the funds into factories and machinery to expand local production capacity. The rise reflects a broader push by domestic drugmakers to scale up manufacturing rather than rely on imports.

stories.h: Dangote Sinotruk unveils first locally assembled electric trucks in Africa
stories.e: Dangote Sinotruk West Africa, a joint venture between Dangote Group and China's Sinotruk, has rolled out what it calls the first new-energy commercial trucks assembled on the African continent, at a ceremony in Lagos. Sinotruk's president hailed the launch as a milestone for Nigeria's automotive manufacturing and its shift towards cleaner transport, though the firm says real savings will depend on charging infrastructure and electricity costs.

stories.h: Dangote Sinotruk unveils Nigeria's first locally assembled electric truck
stories.e: Dangote Sinotruk West Africa rolled out what it calls Nigeria's first locally assembled electric heavy-duty truck at its Lagos plant, following the joint venture's earlier move into CNG-powered vehicles. Executives from Dangote and Sinotruk said wider adoption will depend on building charging infrastructure and training local technicians.

stories.h: AKK gas pipeline nears completion as Kano firm protests land seizure
stories.e: NNPC says the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano gas pipeline mainline is about 95 per cent complete, with gas due in Abuja before year-end and in Kaduna and Kano by 2027. A Kano manufacturer, A.B. Janruwa Enterprises, says over four hectares of its land were taken for the project's development corridor without formal notice or compensation, a claim the state government disputes.

stories.h: Nigerian drugmakers raise factory investment 81% to N29.26bn
stories.e: Nigeria's five listed pharmaceutical manufacturers lifted combined capital spending by 81 per cent to N29.26 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up from N16.20 billion a year earlier, as they expand local production capacity. MeCure Industries and Fidson Healthcare accounted for the largest share of the new spending, while combined revenue across the five firms grew 17.2 per cent to N220.27 billion. The investment drive is being driven partly by government efforts to boost domestic drug manufacturing and by the exit of multinational firms such as GSK from the market.

stories.h: NUPRC approves 595 well re-entries and 145 new drilling operations as rig count hits 100
stories.e: Nigeria's upstream petroleum regulator, the NUPRC, said it has approved 595 well re-entries and 145 new drilling operations, pushing the country's active rig count to 100 for the first time in years. The commission described the increase as evidence of renewed investor confidence in Nigeria's oil and gas sector following recent reforms. A higher rig count typically signals increased future production and could support government revenue projections tied to oil output.

stories.h: Nigerian industrial goods firms' tax payments surge 99% under new tax law
stories.e: Seven listed Nigerian industrial goods companies, including Dangote Cement, BUA Cement and Beta Glass, paid a combined N271.7 billion in income tax in the first nine months of 2026, almost double the same period last year, as Nigeria's new tax framework took effect from January 2026. Combined pre-tax profit across the group rose 43 per cent to N2.49 trillion, though Dangote Cement's own tax bill fell even as its profit grew.

stories.h: Nigeria to start local production of pharmaceutical ingredients by Q1 2027, FG says
stories.e: The Federal Government says Nigeria will begin manufacturing active pharmaceutical ingredients locally from the first quarter of 2027, with a major pharmaceutical company set to build the production plant. PVAC National Coordinator Mukhtar Abdul announced the plan at the 2026 Joint Annual Review in Abuja, framing it as a move to cut reliance on imports. A 2026 KPMG report found that roughly nine in ten active ingredients and excipients used by Nigerian drug makers are currently imported.

stories.h: Nigerian Breweries, Nestle Nigeria and peers book N129.4bn in fees to foreign parents
stories.e: Nigerian Breweries, Nestle Nigeria and several other consumer goods manufacturers paid a combined N129.4 billion in fees and royalties to their foreign parent companies, according to newly reviewed financial filings. The figures renew questions about how much value locally listed manufacturers retain domestically versus what flows abroad.

stories.h: Dangote Cement suspends proposed London Stock Exchange listing
stories.e: Dangote Cement has put on hold its proposed secondary listing on the London Stock Exchange, citing current market conditions and strategic priorities, after earlier signalling in May and July that London was its preferred venue over Dubai for broadening access to overseas investors. The company said its shares remain listed on the Nigerian Exchange and that the decision does not affect its operations, which span 55 million tonnes of annual production capacity across eleven African countries. Dangote Cement, majority-owned by Aliko Dangote, reported a 31 per cent rise in nine-month profit and revenue of N3.8 trillion.

stories.h: Dangote Cement shelves planned London Stock Exchange listing
stories.e: Dangote Cement has called off its previously announced plan to pursue a secondary listing on the London Stock Exchange, according to BusinessDay. The company has not given detailed public reasons for the reversal, though the move comes amid wider volatility in Nigerian capital markets and corporate listing plans. Dangote Cement remains Nigeria dominant cement producer and a bellwether for the country manufacturing sector.

stories.h: Nigeria's solar panel assembly capacity set to double by 2031 - IEA
stories.e: The International Energy Agency projects that Nigeria will at least double its local solar panel assembly capacity, from roughly 500 megawatts a year currently to more than one gigawatt annually by 2031. The agency cautioned that these early-stage manufacturing ventures are unlikely to significantly reduce Nigeria's heavy reliance on imported solar components within that timeframe.

stories.h: FG unveils plans for three lithium processing factories to cut battery imports
stories.e: Vice-President Kashim Shettima says the federal government plans to build three lithium processing factories, in Nasarawa, Kaduna and Abuja, to help Nigeria move up the critical minerals and battery manufacturing value chain and reduce reliance on imported batteries. He made the announcement at an international conference on the African Continental Free Trade Area, though no investment figures or timeline were given.

stories.h: Why Nigeria's cassava output still fails to feed its factories
stories.e: Despite being the world's largest cassava producer, Nigeria's processors continue to face feedstock shortages, according to findings discussed at an industry roundtable. The gap is attributed to overstated national output figures, low farm yields, high harvesting and transport costs, and the marketing of cheaper derivatives as substitutes for genuine cassava starch. Industry voices say solving the supply, cost and demand problems together is essential to unlocking the crop's industrial potential.

stories.h: Rising energy costs drain N820.7bn from NGX-listed industrial firms
stories.e: Industrial goods companies listed on the Nigerian Exchange spent roughly N820.7 billion on fuel and power in the first nine months of 2026, a 6.3 per cent rise year-on-year that is squeezing profit margins. Cement producers Dangote and BUA account for the bulk of that spending, reflecting continued reliance on self-generated power due to an unreliable national grid. Analysts warn manufacturers are struggling to pass these rising costs on to customers.

stories.h: Indorama commits $261m to a fourth fertiliser production line in Nigeria
stories.e: Indorama has issued a letter of award to South Korea's Daewoo for a new $261 million ammonia-urea line at its Eleme complex near Port Harcourt, a project that would lift the company's installed Nigerian urea capacity by about a third. The expansion comes as Gulf shipping disruptions have pushed global urea prices to multi-year highs.

stories.h: Dangote Cement, BUA spend N797 billion in energy cost
stories.e: Nigeria's two largest cement makers, Dangote Cement and BUA Cement, spent a combined N797.1 billion on fuel and power in the first nine months of 2026, nearly 7% more than a year earlier, as both firms leaned on self-generated electricity to cope with a national grid that failed repeatedly during the year. BUA's energy bill rose more than 21%, far outpacing Dangote's smaller 2% increase.

stories.h: Court adjourns terrorism trial of four alleged IPOB members to December
stories.e: A Federal High Court in Abuja adjourned to 7 December the trial of four men accused of terrorism, kidnapping and the killing of a state security operative, allegedly as members of the proscribed IPOB and its armed wing. All four have pleaded not guilty to the six-count charge.

stories.h: UNICEF says 624,000 children remain out of school in Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara
stories.e: UNICEF's Sokoto field office chief, Michael Juma, said at a World Children's Day briefing that about 624,000 children across the three north-western states are still out of school, even though re-enrolment campaigns have reached only around 68,000 of them so far. He said roughly 98,000 children have joined a literacy and numeracy catch-up programme, but getting the remainder back into classrooms remains the main obstacle.

stories.h: Kano LG chairman denies inciting violence after Amnesty International backlash
stories.e: Responding to Amnesty International's description of him as a danger to society, Gwale council chairman Abubakar Mojo said his viral remarks urging APC supporters to secure polling units had been mistranslated and taken out of context. His spokesperson accused a rival political camp of doctoring the video and asked Amnesty to also investigate an alleged disruption of a rival campaign visit in Bichi.

stories.h: Report shows decline in Boko Haram-linked violence since early 2026
stories.e: A Premium Times review of conflict-monitoring data from ACLED shows that Boko Haram-related violence in Nigeria has eased since peaking in April 2026, even as fighting involving the group intensified across the border in Chad and Cameroon. Analysts cite an informal truce said to have held since June, though the trend has been uneven, with localised flare-ups such as in Adamawas Hong council area.

stories.h: Fresh wave of attacks kills more than 20 in Plateau State in two weeks
stories.e: Gunmen have killed more than 20 people, including farmers, herders and a soldier, in a new wave of attacks across Plateau State's Riyom, Barkin Ladi, Qua'an Pan and Mangu council areas between 3 and 17 November. The violence came months after President Tinubu promised extra security following an earlier deadly attack, and local groups say impunity for past killings is fuelling the continued cycle of farmer-herder violence.

stories.h: Enugu Assembly passes bill capping rent increases, scrapping caution fees
stories.e: The Enugu State House of Assembly has passed the Landlord and Tenant Amendment Bill, which limits rent increases to once every four years and caps subsequent rises at two per cent, or ten per cent where renovation is involved. The bill also creates a refundable tenant bond account managed by the Attorney-General's office to curb exploitation by landlords and agents.

stories.h: UN warns aid cuts are exposing refugees to trafficking and exploitation
stories.e: A study by the UN Refugee Agency and Oxford's Nuffield College found that shrinking humanitarian budgets are leaving refugees more vulnerable to trafficking, child labour and sexual exploitation, citing a 28 per cent rise in detected trafficking cases in Bangladesh's Cox's Bazar camp and severe underfunding of child-protection work in Ethiopia. The researchers said the gap between needs and funding has widened as the United States and other major donors have cut development aid.

stories.h: Reps urge FG to help Nigerian fishers left homeless after Gabon demolitions
stories.e: The House of Representatives asked the federal government to open diplomatic talks with Gabon after authorities there reportedly demolished the homes and businesses of Nigerian fishers, mostly Ilaje people from Ondo State, who had lived along the Gabonese coast for decades. Lawmakers directed the Committees on Foreign Affairs and on Cooperation and Integration in Africa to assess the affected citizens' welfare and report back within 14 legislative days.

stories.h: Akwa Ibom fishing community to petition regulators over recurring oil spills
stories.e: Residents of Ntan Mbat in Akwa Ibom's Ibiono Ibom council area say recurring oil sheens, worst in the rainy season, have cut fish catches and hurt the many households that depend on fishing and fish trading for their livelihoods. Village leaders, after a training session with civic groups, agreed to petition the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, NOSDRA and the National Assembly to investigate suspected old, uncapped oil wells they believe are the source.

stories.h: Gunmen strike Zamfara community again, kill guard, abduct family
stories.e: Bandits attacked the home of a businessman in Sabuwar Kaura, Kaura Namoda local government area of Zamfara State on Monday, killing a security guard and abducting several family members, including children. The raid came just a day after gunmen attacked worshippers at a nearby mosque, killing a senior aide to the state governor among others, deepening concern over the state's worsening insecurity.

stories.h: Gunmen kill nine in night raid on Plateau community despite lifted curfew
stories.e: Suspected bandits killed at least nine people and destroyed homes and food stores in a night attack on Zuwagal community in Mangu local government area of Plateau State, days after authorities lifted a dusk-to-dawn curfew in the area. A community leader said residents had warned security agencies of an impending attack two weeks earlier and demanded that the perpetrators be caught and prosecuted.

stories.h: Visually impaired group protests exclusion from Ondo welfare schemes
stories.e: Members of the Association of Technology Inclined Visually Impaired Persons of Nigeria marched to the Ondo State Ministry of Women Affairs in Akure, demanding official recognition and access to government disability programmes they say they have been shut out of all year. They accused the ministry of favouring a rival association and threatened a bigger protest if their registration documents are not acted on within a week.

stories.h: Lawmaker urges FG not to convert Nnamdi Kanu's life sentence into a death sentence
stories.e: A member of the House of Representatives has appealed to the federal government not to escalate separatist leader Nnamdi Kanu's life imprisonment to a death sentence, warning of the wider implications for reconciliation in the South-East. The intervention keeps Kanu's long-running terrorism case, and the human rights questions around it, in the national spotlight.

stories.h: Tinubu orders release of 78 people arrested over attack on his convoy
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu has directed security agencies to release 78 people detained following an incident in which his motorcade came under attack near a mosque in Abuja. The directive follows public concern over the scale of the arrests and raises questions about due process in handling suspects linked to the president's security.

stories.h: Nine still held after bandits abduct Kaduna villagers in fresh raid
stories.e: Suspected bandits abducted 12 residents of Kurmin Wali in Kaduna State's Kajuru council area on Sunday morning, with three later escaping and nine remaining in captivity. The village head said the latest victims join five people seized in two earlier October raids, bringing those still held to 14, and appealed for stronger security action after officers reportedly left within an hour of responding.

stories.h: Police free 19 Zamfara kidnap victims after 22 days in captivity
stories.e: Police, backed by local hunters and security agencies, rescued 19 women and children abducted from Tungar Haki village in Zamfara after 22 days in a bandit camp. In a separate case in the same state, a three-year-old girl was freed and her paternal aunt arrested over an alleged N10 million ransom demand.

stories.h: Bandits kill APC official, abduct worshippers in Zamfara mosque raid
stories.e: Suspected bandits stormed a mosque in Kaura Namoda, Zamfara State, during dawn prayers on Sunday, killing Nasiru Sani, a supervisor of the APC's voter e-registration exercise, and abducting an unconfirmed number of worshippers before fleeing. The attack is the latest in a string of security breaches in the area this year, including earlier raids that killed security personnel and abducted dozens of residents.

stories.h: Security-related deaths hit 835 in October, highest this year – report
stories.e: A security assessment by SARI Global recorded at least 835 conflict and security-related deaths across Nigeria in October 2026, the deadliest month of the year so far and up sharply from 587 in September. Armed conflict accounted for most of the deaths, with Zamfara, Borno and Taraba among the worst-hit states, including an attack on Taraba's Binnari community that reportedly killed at least 62 people.

stories.h: MSF warns of diphtheria antitoxin shortages as Nigeria passes 1,100 deaths
stories.e: Medecins Sans Frontieres has warned that dwindling stocks of diphtheria antitoxin are forcing its teams in northern Nigeria, including Katsina and Zamfara states, to ration treatment for severely ill patients. A Red Cross situation report citing NCDC figures put this year total at 1,126 deaths and over 28,000 confirmed infections across 26 states and the FCT as of early November, prompting MSF to call on federal and state authorities to speed up the supply of medicines and vaccines.

stories.h: Tuggar condemns 'Afrophobia' in South Africa, calls for Pan-African solidarity
stories.e: Former Foreign Minister Yusuf Tuggar has condemned the targeting of Nigerians and other Black Africans in South Africa, arguing that the term 'Afrophobia' better captures the racial dimension of the hostility than 'xenophobia'. Speaking at a Lagos event on Pan-Africanism, he recalled Nigeria's historical support for the anti-apartheid struggle and urged closer scrutiny of who funds and organises anti-migrant campaigns on social media. He said free movement of labour and deeper economic integration, including through the African Continental Free Trade Area, remain essential to continental unity.

stories.h: African Union launches continental credit rating agency to challenge global assessments
stories.e: The African Union has launched the Africa Credit Rating Agency, based in Mauritius, aiming to assess African governments and companies using local data and expertise rather than relying solely on global agencies. Interim chief executive Sifiso Falala says the agency is in talks with fifteen governments and expects to issue its first sovereign ratings by the end of March, arguing that subjective assessments have cost African nations tens of billions of dollars in higher borrowing costs. Analysts caution its credibility will hinge on maintaining independence, since governments pay for its sovereign ratings.

stories.h: China, US and Russia issue joint 'Declaration Toward Peace' after historic summit
stories.e: Presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin held an unprecedented trilateral summit in Shenzhen, China, after which the three powers issued a joint statement setting out shared ambitions to reform the United Nations and curb the reach of the International Criminal Court. European leaders including Germany's Friedrich Merz and France's Emmanuel Macron were dismissive of the talks, even as Trump and Putin both described the meeting as historic.

stories.h: Ghana's public debt jumps 32% to $65.3 billion under Mahama
stories.e: Ghana's public debt has risen by 32 per cent to $65.3 billion in under two years under President John Mahama's administration, according to new figures. The sharp increase raises questions about fiscal management in one of West Africa's largest economies, with implications for regional economic stability.

stories.h: Activist warns COP31 carbon removal push could hurt African farmland and fisheries
stories.e: Kwami Kpondzo of the Global Forest Coalition has warned that carbon dioxide removal technologies being pushed at the COP31 climate talks could worsen food insecurity and strain African smallholder farmers and fishing communities. He argued that large-scale bioenergy and ocean-based removal schemes let big polluters avoid cutting emissions at source, and that climate finance should not be diverted from adaptation support that developing nations, including Nigeria, are owed.

stories.h: Nigeria reviews report on diplomatic row with South Africa over livestream
stories.e: Nigeria's foreign ministry says it is reviewing a report on a diplomatic spat after its High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, accused Pretoria of cutting the livestream of his credentials speech, a claim South African officials deny. Pretoria summoned Fani-Kayode over the public complaint, which it says breached diplomatic protocol, straining relations between the two African countries.

stories.h: Eight Nigerians among twelve arrested in Canada over $4.5m car theft ring
stories.e: Police in Ontario, Canada, arrested eight Nigerians and four others accused of running a syndicate that stole and disguised high-value vehicles for export to West Africa. Investigators recovered 96 vehicles worth about $4.5 million hidden in shipping containers, and the suspects face 231 charges in total.

stories.h: South Africa summons Nigerian envoy over livestream row
stories.e: South Africa's foreign ministry summoned Nigeria's High Commissioner, Femi Fani-Kayode, accusing him of breaching diplomatic protocol after he publicly alleged that his credential-presentation speech had been deliberately cut from the presidential livestream. South African officials and the public broadcaster rejected the claim, and both sides later described their meeting as cordial, even as the incident added fresh strain to relations already tense since deadly anti-Nigerian violence in April.

stories.h: COP31: Observers raise concerns as presidencies publish first draft of cover decision
stories.e: Civil society observers at the COP31 climate summit have criticised the first draft of the conference's cover decision, arguing it falls short on ambition for emissions cuts and climate finance. The concerns echo long-standing complaints from African delegations, including Nigeria's, that wealthier nations are not matching their climate pledges with adequate funding.

stories.h: Seventeen killed in separate overnight shootings across South Africa
stories.e: Seventeen people were shot dead in two unconnected incidents in South Africa on Sunday night, eight men killed inside a minibus in KwaZulu-Natal and nine others, including three women, shot inside a shack near Pretoria. Police say no suspects have been identified and have launched manhunts, as the country continues to grapple with gun violence that claimed nearly 5,500 lives between April and June alone.

stories.h: Nigeria's mission in South Africa urges calm after row over Ramaphosa spokesman's remarks
stories.e: Nigeria's High Commission in South Africa has called for restraint after President Cyril Ramaphosa's spokesperson accused Nigerian envoy Femi Fani-Kayode of lying about Ramaphosa's intervention in a dispute over a disrupted livestream of his credentialing ceremony. The Nigerian mission said the matter should be handled through diplomatic channels and declared the issue closed, while warning it was ready to respond further if South Africa chose to escalate.

stories.h: Ebola cases in DR Congo surpass 11,000 as insecurity hampers response
stories.e: The World Health Organisation says confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo have passed 11,000, with over 5,400 deaths, as armed attacks on health facilities and workers continue to disrupt containment efforts. Nigeria's own imported case has recovered and all 62 traced contacts completed monitoring without further infection, though the NCDC cautions the outbreak is not yet officially over.

stories.h: AfDB and Japan's JICA sign $583 million deal to fund Africa's poorest countries
stories.e: The African Development Bank and the Japan International Cooperation Agency have signed a concessional loan agreement worth roughly $583 million to support the African Development Fund's seventeenth replenishment. Signed in Tokyo by AfDB president Sidi Ould Tah and JICA president Akihiko Tanaka, it is described as Japan's largest-ever assistance package to the Fund, aimed at infrastructure, energy access and food security in low-income African states. The replenishment round overall raised a record $11 billion from 44 partners.

stories.h: Cabo Verde votes as incumbent president seeks second term
stories.e: Cabo Verdeans went to the polls to elect a president, with incumbent José Maria Neves, who took office in 2021, seeking a second term against several challengers including Joana Rosa of the opposition MpD. A runoff is scheduled for 29 November if no candidate wins an outright majority in the first round.

stories.h: Nigeria proposes $10 billion African Union Peace Fund
stories.e: Nigeria has proposed a $10 billion African Union Peace Fund to be built up over the next decade, aiming to cut the bloc's reliance on external funding for peace and security operations. Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele put the proposal to an AU Executive Council session in Accra, suggesting the fund draw on member levies and African capital while its principal is preserved and only the interest spent.

stories.h: Nigeria and South Africa trade accusations over cut diplomatic livestream
stories.e: A public row has broken out between Nigeria and South Africa after Nigeria's High Commissioner, Femi Fani-Kayode, accused Pretoria of cutting the livestream of his speech while presenting his credentials to President Cyril Ramaphosa. South Africa's presidency denied controlling the broadcast, prompting Nigeria's High Commission to publicly call the presidential spokesperson a liar, in the latest flare-up following earlier tensions over xenophobic attacks on Nigerians.

stories.h: Nigeria joins 150 countries backing UN resolution on Palestinian resources
stories.e: Nigeria was among roughly 150 countries that adopted a United Nations General Assembly resolution affirming Palestinian sovereignty over natural resources in the occupied territories. The vote reflects Nigeria's continuing diplomatic support for Palestinian self-determination at multilateral forums.

stories.h: Nigeria and South Africa trade accusations over envoy's cut-off livestream
stories.e: Nigeria's new high commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, accused Pretoria of cutting the livestream of his speech at his own credentials ceremony, while South African presidential spokesman Vincent Magwenya denied this and accused him of misrepresentation. The row adds to friction between the two countries following xenophobic attacks that have been linked to the deaths of at least 12 Nigerians since April.

stories.h: South Sudan delays first post-independence elections again
stories.e: South Sudans electoral commission has pushed back the countrys first national elections since independence from 22 December 2026 to 11 February 2027, the second such postponement. The delay comes amid rising tension between President Salva Kiirs camp and supporters of his rival Riek Machar, who has been under house arrest since March 2025 facing treason and murder charges. The UNs human rights body has separately warned that the safeguards needed for a credible vote are still not in place.

stories.h: Fani-Kayode presents credentials to Ramaphosa, begins duty as envoy to South Africa
stories.e: Femi Fani-Kayode formally began his assignment as Nigeria's High Commissioner to South Africa, presenting his Letter of Credence to President Cyril Ramaphosa in Pretoria alongside envoys from 14 other countries. He invoked Nigeria's support for South Africa during the anti-apartheid era and said his task was to reset bilateral ties, but complained that South African state media had livestreamed every other new ambassador's remarks except his. The ceremony comes amid persistent strain between the two countries over xenophobic violence against Nigerian migrants, with Fani-Kayode previously estimating that South African police have killed at least 30 Nigerians over the past four years.

stories.h: Nigeria and EU sign deal to facilitate return of irregular migrants
stories.e: Nigeria and the European Union have signed an agreement intended to make it easier to return Nigerians living in Europe without valid immigration status. The deal forms part of broader migration cooperation between Abuja and Brussels.

stories.h: CAF unveils official logo for 2027 Africa Cup of Nations
stories.e: The Confederation of African Football and host nations Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda have jointly unveiled the official emblem for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, simultaneously launched in all three countries. The design, built around a traditional East African shield with the tournament trophy at its centre, is meant to represent the shared heritage and identity of the three co-hosts ahead of the continental tournament.

stories.h: FIFA president Infantino visits Warri, pledges support for Nigerian football
stories.e: FIFA president Gianni Infantino visited Warri in Delta State ahead of the unveiling of the newly reconstructed Warri City Stadium, praising the state's investment in grassroots football. Governor Sheriff Oborevwori's administration rebuilt the stadium, which officials say is intended to boost football development across the Niger Delta.

stories.h: FIFA president Infantino tours renovated Warri City Stadium ahead of commissioning
stories.e: FIFA president Gianni Infantino visited Delta State to inspect the newly rebuilt Warri City Stadium ahead of its formal commissioning, which is expected to be attended by CAF president Patrice Motsepe. Infantino praised the facility and argued that developing smaller, community-level stadiums matters as much to footballs growth as hosting major tournaments, as part of Delta States wider investment in sporting infrastructure.

stories.h: National Sports Commission postpones Enugu 2026 festival to May 2027
stories.e: Nigeria's National Sports Commission has approved postponing the Enugu 2026 National Sports Festival to May 2027. The Local Organising Committee cited circumstances beyond the Enugu State Government's control, delaying one of the country's major multi-sport events.

stories.h: FIFA appoints five-member Normalisation Committee to run NFF until May 2027
stories.e: FIFA has installed a five-member Normalisation Committee, chaired by former League Management Company lawyer Samson Ebomhe and including ex-international Daniel Amokachi, to run the Nigeria Football Federation's affairs with immediate effect. The committee, which also features Godwin Enakhena, Joe Abah and Amina Yerima, must review the NFF's statutes and electoral code, push wider stakeholder representation, and oversee fresh leadership elections before its mandate ends in May 2027. Members are barred from contesting those elections themselves, and the outgoing NFF administration has been told to cooperate fully with the takeover.

stories.h: CAF president Motsepe arrives in Abuja for general assembly
stories.e: CAF president Patrice Motsepe arrived in Abuja ahead of the 48th CAF Ordinary General Assembly, which Nigeria is hosting for the first time in 17 years. The gathering brings together officials from CAF's 54 member associations, alongside the FIFA president, days before Nigeria also hosts the CAF Awards in Lagos.

stories.h: Super Eagles climb to 29th in FIFA world rankings, fifth in Africa
stories.e: Nigeria's Super Eagles rose one place to 29th in the latest FIFA world rankings, moving above Algeria into fifth place in Africa, after a 3-1 win over Tanzania was followed by a goalless draw in the reverse fixture. The gain reflects Algeria's decline as much as Nigeria's own form, with coach Eric Chelle still working to find consistency ahead of the 2027 AFCON qualifiers.

stories.h: Super Eagles held to goalless draw by Tanzania in AFCON qualifying setback
stories.e: Nigeria's Super Eagles were held 0-0 by Tanzania's Taifa Stars in Zanzibar, missing the chance to build on their first-leg win in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers. Coach Eric Chelle's side struggled to convert chances despite periods of control, leaving work to do in the remaining qualifying fixtures.

stories.h: Super Eagles held to goalless draw by Tanzania in AFCON qualifier
stories.e: Nigeria’s Super Eagles were held to a 0-0 draw by Tanzania in Zanzibar in their latest 2027 AFCON qualifying fixture, despite having won the reverse leg 3-1 in Uyo. The result leaves Nigeria level on seven points with Guinea-Bissau at the top of Group L, with only the group winner guaranteed a place at the finals. The draw raises pressure on the team to improve its finishing in the remaining qualifiers.

stories.h: Abia dissolves Enyimba management amid relegation battle
stories.e: The Abia State Government has dissolved Enyimba International's management and technical crew after the storied club slipped to 18th place in the Nigeria Premier Football League following 13 matches. Officials cited administrative and structural problems and said the Ministry of Sports and Youth Development would take over running the club while a restructuring plan is worked out.

stories.h: Tanzania hold Super Eagles to goalless draw in AFCON qualifier
stories.e: Nigeria's Super Eagles were held 0-0 by Tanzania in Zanzibar in their 2027 AFCON qualifying return leg, missing several chances including a crossbar strike from Tolu Arokodare. The draw leaves Nigeria level on points with Group L leaders Guinea-Bissau, and under pressure to improve their finishing with qualification for the tournament still not secured.

stories.h: Super Eagles face Tanzania in Zanzibar return leg after 3-1 first-leg win
stories.e: Nigerias Super Eagles travel to Zanzibar to face Tanzania in the return leg of their 2027 AFCON qualifying double-header, four days after winning the first leg 3-1 in Uyo. Captain Wilfred Ndidi anchors midfield again, while coach Eric Chelle has flagged forward Ademola Lookmans knee as the main fitness concern heading into the match.

stories.h: Super Eagles chase Tanzania double in Zanzibar after Uyo win
stories.e: Having beaten Tanzania 3-1 in Uyo on 13 November, Nigeria's Super Eagles travel to Zanzibar's Amaan Stadium for the reverse fixture in their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign. Coach Eric Chelle's squad, missing regulars such as Victor Osimhen and Kelechi Iheanacho, will be looking to consolidate their position in Group L against hosts already assured of a place at next year's tournament.

stories.h: Olympic Eagles face uphill task against DR Congo in Ikenne return leg
stories.e: Nigeria's Olympic Eagles must overturn a 2-0 first-leg deficit against DR Congo in Tuesday's return leg of their 2027 CAF U-23 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier in Ikenne-Remo, needing at least a three-goal margin to progress without penalties. The winner advances to face Burkina Faso or Zambia, with qualification also carrying a route to the men's football event at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

stories.h: Super Eagles beat Tanzania 3-1 in Uyo ahead of AFCON 2027 decider
stories.e: Nigeria's Super Eagles defeated Tanzania 3-1 in Uyo in their AFCON 2027 qualifier, with Tolu Arokodare scoring twice after Alhassan Yusuf's early opener, despite Alphonce Msanga's equaliser for the visitors. The result leaves Nigeria on six points in Group L, one behind leaders Guinea-Bissau, with the final qualification place still open since co-hosts Tanzania had already qualified. The squad has since travelled to Zanzibar for the return fixture, though star forward Ademola Lookman will miss it with a knee ligament injury.

stories.h: Awoniyi says AFCON qualification "non-negotiable" ahead of Tanzania return leg
stories.e: Super Eagles striker Taiwo Awoniyi says securing Nigeria's place at the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations is essential "no matter what", as the team travelled to Tanzania for a decisive qualifier. Nigeria currently sit second in their qualifying group with three matches left to play.

stories.h: Nigeria beat Tanzania 3-1 to revive 2027 AFCON qualifying hopes
stories.e: The Super Eagles came from behind to beat Tanzania 3-1 in Uyo, with Tolu Arokodare scoring twice after coming off the bench, lifting Nigeria to within a point of Group L leaders Guinea-Bissau in the race for a single 2027 AFCON qualifying slot. The sides meet again in Zanzibar on 17 November.

stories.h: Flamingos say World Cup triumph is just the beginning as players eye Europe
stories.e: Members of Nigeria's Under-17 women's team, the Flamingos, say their recent FIFA Under-17 Women's World Cup win in Morocco is only a starting point, with captain Chidi Harmony and Golden Ball winner Oluebube Umejiaku both saying they want to build on it with moves to leading European clubs. Players also called for greater investment in Nigeria's domestic women's league to support the next generation of talent.

stories.h: Arokodare's double sends Super Eagles past Tanzania in AFCON qualifier
stories.e: Substitute striker Tolu Arokodare scored twice as Nigeria came from behind to beat Tanzania 3-1 in Uyo in their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier, with Alhassan Yusuf opening the scoring before Tanzania briefly levelled. The win keeps the Super Eagles' qualification hopes alive ahead of the return leg in Zanzibar.

stories.h: DR Congo beat Nigeria's Olympic Eagles 2-0 in U-23 AFCON qualifier first leg
stories.e: Nigeria's Olympic Eagles suffered a 2-0 defeat to DR Congo in Lubumbashi in the first leg of their 2027 Africa U-23 Cup of Nations qualifier, leaving them needing to overturn the deficit in the return leg. Samuel James turned the ball into his own net early on before Filozofe Mabete added a second with a free kick, with Nigeria's Zadok Yohanna forced off injured. The return leg takes place on 17 November at the Remo Stars Stadium in Ikenne, Ogun State, with the winner securing a route to the 2027 U-23 AFCON in Egypt and onward Olympic qualification.
